Let \(m=\binom n2\). The Smith normal form is
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{diag}\Bigl(
\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{n},
\,4,\,
\underbrace{2n,\ldots,2n}_{m-n-1},
\underbrace{2n(n+1),\ldots,2n(n+1)}_{n-1},
\,0
\Bigr)
}
\]
for every even \(n\ge 6\).

Here is the derivation. Interpret \(L_n\) as a presentation matrix with generators \(x_i\) for vertices and \(y_{ij}\) for unordered pairs. Make the unimodular change of generators
\[
z_{ij}=y_{ij}-x_i-x_j.
\]
Writing \(s=\sum_i x_i\) and \(Z_i=\sum_{j\ne i}z_{ij}\), the relations become
\[
(n+1)x_i-2s-Z_i=0,
\qquad
2n z_{ij}+2s=0.
\]
Thus the transformed presentation matrix is
\[
M=
\begin{pmatrix}
(n+1)I_n-2J_n&-B_n\\
2\mathbf 1_{m\times n}&2nI_m
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

It is enough to compute the Smith form prime-locally.

If \(p\mid 2n\), then \(n+1\) and \(n-1\) are units in \(\mathbb Z_{(p)}\), and
\[
(n+1)I_n-2J_n
\]
is invertible over \(\mathbb Z_{(p)}\). Taking the Schur complement gives a \(p\)-local equivalent matrix
\[
2nI_m-\frac4{n-1}J_m.
\]
Multiplying by the unit \(n-1\), this is equivalent to
\[
4(mI_m-J_m),
\qquad m=\frac{n(n-1)}2.
\]
Since \(mI_m-J_m\) has Smith form
\[
\operatorname{diag}(1,\underbrace{m,\ldots,m}_{m-2},0),
\]
the \(p\)-part is
\[
4,\quad \underbrace{2n,\ldots,2n}_{m-2}
\]
because \(4m=2n(n-1)\) and \(n-1\) is a \(p\)-local unit.

If \(p\mid n+1\), then \(2n\) is a unit. Taking the other Schur complement gives
\[
(n+1)I_n-\frac{n+1}{n}J_n
=\frac{n+1}{n}(nI_n-J_n).
\]
Since \(n\) is a \(p\)-local unit and
\[
nI_n-J_n
\]
has Smith form
\[
\operatorname{diag}(1,\underbrace{n,\ldots,n}_{n-2},0),
\]
the \(p\)-part contributes \(n-1\) copies of \(n+1\).

The factors \(2n\) and \(n+1\) are coprime. Combining the local data in divisibility order gives one extra factor \(4\), then \(m-n-1\) factors \(2n\), and pairs the remaining \(n-1\) factors \(2n\) with the \(n-1\) factors \(n+1\). The matrix has rank \(n+m-1\), so there is one final zero and \(n\) unit invariant factors. Thus the Smith normal form is exactly
\[
\operatorname{diag}\Bigl(
1^{\,n},\,
4,\,
(2n)^{\,m-n-1},\,
(2n(n+1))^{\,n-1},\,
0
\Bigr).
\]
